newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed, Brent CFDs soar but jet dives.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed, Brent CFDs soar but jet dives.

text.p: European oil swaps mostly extended recent gains on Friday with Brent crude moving into backwardation amid fears that next month's North Sea crude supplies might be lower than expected.
But jet took a dive with physical traders selling levels down $1 to $2 a tonne against the IPE gas oil contract.
Brent crude futures levered into backwardation between June and July pulling CFDs sharply higher.
Weekly CFDs jumped around 15 cents a barrel with trade at just 8 cents under July compared to levels around 23 cents under on Thursday.
The following weeks moved into backwardation with the May 19-23 week at 12 cents under and May 27-30 at 14 cents under.

Monthly CFDs also moved quickly higher with offers virtually impossible to find as inter-month spreads rose quickly again. The balance of May and June were both talked around 15 cents under the screen although forward levels stayed in contango.
The forward curve was valued against front line IPE Brent at -15 cents (July), -13 cts (3Q97), -10 cts (4Q97), -5 cts (1Q98), -4 (2Q98) and -6 cents for the whole of 1998.

Fuel swaps climbed another $1 a tonne for the third successive session. May barge swaps rose to $86, tugged higher by rampant Singapore prices and some demand in the Mediterranean. Singapore rose to $103 for May and $101.50 for June.
Rotterdam barges rose $3 but fell back to $85 having traded briskly between $86 and $87 during the morning.

Further forward the contango was showing signs of flattening out. The third to fourth quarter contango fell to $4.50 a tonne from $5.50 on Wednesday. The two quarters were valued at $87 and $91.50 respectively.
Gasoline also firmed $1 a tonne but activity remained thin with muted local demand in Rotterdam. June rose $3 a tonne to $197 but May only edged up $1.50 to the same level.
Jet premiums sunk $1 to $2 a tonne with May and June falling to just 420 above the IPE and next week trading at $29 above the screen, well below recent levels of about $31 above.
Gas oil crack spreads held at $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.85 (4Q97) and $4.70 (1Q98).
